question: A circular wheel is divided into 8 equal sectors. If the area of one sector is 45 cm², what is the radius of the wheel?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total area of the wheel = Area of 1 sector × Number of sectors

⇒ Total area = 45 × 8 = 360 cm²

Area of a circle = πr² = 360

⇒ r² = 360 × (7 ÷ 22) = 114.54

⇒ r = √114.54 ≈ 10.7 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 10.7 cm.**

**Given:**

Number of equal sectors in the wheel = 8

Area of one sector = 45 cm²

**Formula Used:**

Total Area of a circle = πr²

Total Area = Area of one sector × Total number of sectors

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Area of the wheel = 45 × 8 = 360 cm²

⇒ πr² = 360

⇒ (22 ÷ 7) × r² = 360

⇒ r² = (360 × 7) ÷ 22

⇒ r² = 2520 ÷ 22 = 114.54

⇒ r = √114.54

⇒ r ≈ 10.7 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 10.7 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of a Sector

The area of a sector of a circle with radius r and central angle θ (in degrees) is given by Area = (θ ÷ 360°) × πr².

Length of an Arc

The length of an arc that subtends an angle θ at the center is given by L = (θ ÷ 360°) × 2πr.

Central Angle of Equal Sectors

When a circle is divided into 'n' equal sectors, the central angle of each sector formed is θ = 360° ÷ n.
